Many vendors provide access to a suite of quantum hardware with varied qubit technologies, number of qubits, cou-pling architectures, and noise characteristics. However, present QML algorithms do not use them for the training procedure and often rely on local noiseless/noisy simulators due to cost and training timing overhead on real hardware. Taking these constraints into account, we perform a study to maximize the inferencing performance of QML workloads based on the choice of hardware selection. Specifically, we perform a detailed analysis of quantum classifiers (both training and inference through the lens of hardware queue wait times) on Iris and reduced Digits datasets under noise and varied conditions such as different hardware and coupling maps. We show that using multiple readily available hardware for training rather than relying on a single hardware, especially if it has a long queue depth of pending jobs, can lead to a performance impact of only 3–4 % while providing up to 45X reduction in training wait time.

title: HyCMAx: Power-Efficient Hybrid CMOS-Memristor Based Approximate Dividers for Error-Resilient Applications
abstract: Approximate computing is a promising paradigm for improving the performance parameters of electronic systems at the expense of accuracy in error-resilient tasks such as multimedia processing, image multiplication, and neural networks. While approximate circuits utilizing CMOS technology have been extensively studied, integrating approximate computing with emerging technologies like memristors offers further performance enhancements. HyCMAx investigates a hybrid CMOS-memristor approach for designing approximate circuits. In this paper, an approximate subtractor has been proposed, which was subsequently used to implement a restoring divider using the hybrid CMOS-memristor approach. HyCMAx dividers implemented in 28nm CMOS technology node gave up to ~43.8% dynamic power reduction and ~31.3% transistor count reduction as compared to only-CMOS implementation. Different levels of approximation were introduced in the divider to study the limits of approximation, which would give acceptable results. The proposed designs were then evaluated in the context of neural networks and image processing applications. This study highlights the potential of combining CMOS and memristor technologies to create high-performance, power-efficient approximate circuits suitable for various error-resilient computational tasks.

title: Advancing Functional Safety: Improving Failure Mode Analysis and Fault Injection Using Automation and GNN Algorithms
abstract: High-Reliability systems need protective measure to ensure functional safety. Traditionally, Failure Mode Analysis (FMA) and Fault Injection (FI) methodologies have been key components in ensuring the functional safety of these systems. However, the ever-increasing complexity of electronic systems poses significant challenges in the efficient and consistent implementation of FMA and FI processes. The challenges include identifying susceptible modules in a short time during FMA, high simulation time, manual effort and resource requirement during FI. To address these challenges, this paper presents two innovative solutions. First, we introduce a FMA automation system that ensures consistency across modules, while significantly reducing effort. Second, we propose a machine learning-based solution to enhance the FI process. Specifically, we leverage Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to accelerate the detection of critical nodes. Our novel application of the GCNII model overcomes the limitations of traditional Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) in handling complex designs with higher logic depth. The employed technique showed increased accuracy and capabilities in forecasting fault criticality. Consequently, this paper facilitates the development of reliable and functionally safe electronic systems.

title: A 0.27-THz Frequency Multiplier Chain Using Harmonic Mixing with Multiplication of × 18 in 65-nm CMOS
abstract: This paper presents a 0.27 THz frequency multiplier chain with higher harmonic rejection (HRR) and a multiplication factor of × 18 using harmonic mixing. The multiplier chain is designed in a 65nm CMOS process. It comprises two triplers (×3) and one doubler (×2). A tail inductor is placed at the common mode node of the first tripler to increase the third harmonic content. In the second tripler, capacitive neutralization is used for fundamental rejection and to increase the gain at 135 GHz, increasing the harmonic rejection ratio (HRR) at the output. The inter-stage buffers are optimized for harmonic amplification and filtering of unwanted harmonics. A push-push doubler is used as the last stage multiplier. The post layout (EM simulation of passives and parasitic extraction of transistors) simulation result of the proposed frequency multiplier has an HRR of greater than 30 dBc and saturated output power of -0.93 dBm with -4 dBm input power and peak conversion gain of 11.2 dB at -14 dBm input power. It consumes 134 mW of DC power from a 1.2 V supply and covers 43 GHz bandwidth from 247–290 GHz.

title: Atrial Flutter Detection System by AdEx Encoded Lead-II ECG
abstract: Quantitatively characterizing atrial electrical activity during irregular heart rhythms, such as atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL), is challenging. In this work, a novel time-domain system for detecting AFL has been implemented using a Spiking Neuron Model on an FPGA. This approach leverages a biologically plausible AdEx neuron model to encode the data. Parameters such as Individual Flutter Width (IFW) and Atrial Cycle Length (ACL) were extracted from the encoded spikes. The system was tested with ECG signals corresponding to Modified Lead-II (ML-II) from the MIT-BIH database, achieving sensitivities of 92% for record 202 from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database and 88% for record 04043 from the MIT-BIH Atrial Fibrillation Database.

title: FPUGen: A FrameWork to Generate Custom Floating Point FMA Accelerators on FPGAs
abstract: Floating-point representations enable finer granularity of computations, improving the overall accuracy of ML models. Approximate computing techniques using variable bit-width can be employed to reduce the computational complexity of training algorithms while maintaining an acceptable level of accuracy. In this work, we propose FPUGen: a framework to generate custom floating-point (FP) fused multiply-add (FMA) accelerators. The accelerators have several architectural highlights such as: (a) Reconfigurable FP-FMA units for any mantissa and exponent size, (b) Dynamic precision FMA (DFMA) support for one SP-32, two TF-32, two HP-16, or three BF-16 operations in parallel, (c) Rounding logic for dynamic precision and (d) pipelined/non-pipelined FP-FMA architecture support. We note that choosing BF-16 over DP-64 and SP-32 saves energy by 5.73x and 2.56x respectively on an FPGA. Our proposed DFMA-V2 architecture is 1.49x more resource efficient, has 3.85x better throughput, and is 1.71x more energy efficient compared to the baseline design (DFMA-V1) due to the pipelined and resource-sharing architecture. It achieves a maximum throughput of 56.10 GFLOP/s on the ZCU104 FPGA, which is 5.8x higher than the baseline design.

title: Layer-Specific Hardware Pooling Designs for CNN Accelerators
abstract: This paper proposes and explores the impact of using Combinatorial Pooling techniques - the combination of widely used Max pooling and SOTA Deviation based pooling techniques such as Absolute Average Deviation (AAD) or Binary Weighted Absolute Deviation (BWAD) or Absolute Maximum Deviation (AMD), across different layers in CNN architectures. The design-space exploration suggests the best possible combination of pooling schemes to be adopted for realizing hardware-efficient CNN accelerators in the future. The proposed Combinatorial pooling schemes offer enhanced model accuracy in AlexNet, UNet, and VGG-16 CNN architectures, besides offering substantial hardware gains, when compared to sole usage of deviation based pooling techniques. The results obtained from FPGA synthesis on Xilinx Zedboard are presented for a single cumulative unit of convolution and pooling operation for Max, AAD, BWAD and AMD methods. ASIC Synthesis results using Cadence 45 nm technology library are showcased for exhaustive combinations when implemented for all convolution and pooling layers in VGG-16 and AlexNet CNN architectures. For AlexNet, the unique sequence “110” with BWAD (BWAD-BWAD-Max), offers footprint savings of 4.27%, 14.77%, 11.87%, and 14.64%, over the regular individual pooling methods of Max, AAD, BWAD and AMD respectively. It also exhibits 6.67% increase in accuracy over the SOTA best.

title: Enhancing Reliability and Energy Efficiency in Network-on-Chip Architectures through Hybrid Sorting Algorithm-Based Core Mapping
abstract: Reliability and energy efficiency are critical challenges in the design of modern Network-on-Chip (NoC) architectures, where the efficient mapping of computational tasks to processing cores plays a pivotal role in overall system performance. To address these challenges, A hybrid sorting algorithm-based core mapping strategy that combines Bitonic and Selection sorters has been proposed. The Bitonic sorter is employed for high-throughput, parallel sorting of task sequences, ensuring an efficient initial task placement. Subsequently, the Selection sorter refines the mapping by focusing on core reliability and energy efficiency, operating in a dual-mode that adapts to varying workload demands. This hybrid approach significantly reduces communication overhead, minimizes energy consumption, and enhances the overall reliability of NoC systems. A Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) was used to measure performance metrics such as application runtime, area, and onchip power consumption. Experimental results using synthetic and real-world benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, showcasing its potential to optimize task-to-core mappings for next-generation NoC designs,

title: 8GHz Multi-Phase Ring VCO Design with Wide Tuning Range for SerDes Applications in 6nm FinFET Process
abstract: In this paper the design of 8-phase, 8GHz pseudo Differential Ring Oscillator (DRO), in 6nm FinFET process technology with a supply voltage of 0.8V ± 5% and temperature range of −40°C to +125°C, is shown. Two Basic Delay Cells (BDC-l and BDC-2) are proposed and the performance of the DROs, using the two BDCs, are compared with architectures from the literature. The DROs, using BDC-l and BDC-2, have wide Frequency Tuning Range (FTR) of 4GHz (from 9.5GHz to 5.5GHz) and 3.29GHz (from 9.29GHz to 6GHz) with a Phase Noise (PN) of −78.43dBc/Hz and −83.41dBc/Hz @ 1MHz offset from the carrier frequency, respectively under nominal PVT conditions. The input control Voltage Tuning Range (VTR) is approximately from 0.16V to 0.64V (i.e., 20% to 80% of the nominal supply voltage). The BDC-l and BDC-2 based DROs have an average power of 19.5mW and 25.6mW respectively.

title: BMC Engine Sequencing with Graph Neural Network Embeddings of Hardware Circuits
abstract: In recent times, the rise of deep learning models has fostered the adoption of machine learning in several facets of the Electronic Design Automation (EDA) life cycle. In particular, in the area of design verification, learning-based representations have yielded great benefits in enriching verification performance and enhancing the performance limits of verification tools. In this paper, we use neural graph embeddings of hardware circuits to expedite the performance of Bounded Model Checking (BMC), which is an important technology for Formal Verification (FV) today. Given a hardware circuit for verification, we use Graph Neural Network (GNN) embeddings produced by a circuit representation learning tool DeepGate2 to facilitate the BMC task. We address the problem of engine switching in BMC to harness the best benefits at different depths. Experimental results on the HWMCC benchmarks show the efficacy of our proposal.

title: Boosting System-on-Chip Performance Through AI-Assisted Optimization Using Compositional Neural Networks
abstract: System-on-Chip performance verification and optimization at pre-silicon level is a complex task that involves tuning multiple parameters, including clock frequency, voltage supply, routing constraints etc., to meet performance targets. Traditional manual optimization methods are time-consuming, error-prone, and lead to sub-optimal results and significant design iterations. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel AI-assisted SOC performance optimization framework that leverages the power of compositionality of Artificial Neural Networks. The proposed framework consists of three stages. In the first stage, neural models at different component/cluster interfaces are developed and trained on a large dataset of a given SOC with respective performance metrics to predict their performance based on their design parameters. In the second stage, the neural networks at every interface guide a search algorithm to find optimal design configuration values for a given performance target. Finally, SOC level compositional neural network is implemented using all the interface level parameters for the design. The proposed framework's novelty lies in the use of compositionality of ANNs, that capture complex relationships between the design parameters and performance metrics. This approach reduces training time and enables the optimization of complex SOC designs. Finally, the accuracy of such composed neural models ensures that our compositional technique is efficient and hence provides a promising solution in addressing the challenges of SOC performance optimization, with improved performance and reduced SOC validation time.

title: Design of Manchester Carry Chain Hybrid Adder for MASH 1-1-1 Delta Sigma Modulator for Fractional-N Frequency Synthesizers
abstract: This paper presents the design of a dynamic hybrid adder for high speed, low-power MASH 1-1-1 Delta Sigma Modulator (DSM), which is commonly used in low noise fractional-N frequency synthesizers. The proposed high-speed hybrid adder architecture employs Carry-Look-Ahead and Carry-Select adders to achieve superior worst-case delay performance as compared to the previously reported works. Implementation of the proposed hybrid adder utilizes Domino Logic style and Manchester Carry Chain adder topology. Additionally, a negative-edge triggered partially static, low-power, high-speed hybrid flip-flop is also presented to sample the adder output before its pre-charge phase. The proposed designs have been simulated and synthesized in Verilog using Xilinx Vivado 2024.1 on Zedboard. Mash 1-1-1 DSM design with the proposed adder is also implemented in TSMC 65nm CMOS technology. Simulation results show that the proposed adder achieves a worst-case delay of 181.9 ps and an average power consumption of 202.52 μW, at a clock frequency of 100 MHz. The Mash 1-1-1 DSM design, utilizing the proposed adder, was simulated to achieve specific average values at a clock frequency of 100 MHz across various process and temperature variations and compared with measured average values.

title: Constructing Rectilinear Steiner Minimum Tree with Conditional Generative Adversarial Network
abstract: Given n points in the 2D plane which are the pins of a net, a Rectilinear Steiner Minimum Tree (RSMT) which consists only of vertical and horizontal line segments is the shortest network to interconnect the pins along with a few extra (Steiner) points. An RSMT for a net has a minimum total wirelength in Manhattan distance and acts as a backbone to many state-of-the-art global routers. However, finding an RSMT is NPcomplete. In this work, we propose a method for constructing an RSMT with an image-to-image translation using a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) based model. Images of RSMTs with optimal wirelength for randomly generated nets form our training dataset. Experimental results show that, after training, our model generates RSMTs with $\leq 0.348\%$ wirelength error on average compared with the optimal solution for nets with degrees up to 50. This is the first successful attempt to solve the RSMT construction problem as an image-to-image translation problem using a cGAN based model.

title: Physical Synthesis Optimization Prediction Using Machine Learning
abstract: Early availability of estimated values of critical Power-Performance-Area [PPA] parameters which are known only after end of EDA tool run, can be of immense value in accelerating design convergence effort in complex SOC designs. Long tool runtime acts as bottleneck for design turn-around-time as well as engineering productivity. AI/ML can be a game changer in this direction with high potential of predicting these key parameters before/parallel to actual tool-based runs once trained on a rich dataset. An early work is demonstrated in physical synthesis domain using supervised Machine Learning where a model can predict relevant PPA component data such as Timing slack, Critical Path Depth, Leakage Power, Area among others within 6-10% typical accuracy. This study is based on sub10nm SOC design implementation dataset operating at typical clock speed of 1 GHz.

title: Interconnect Optimization for Timing and Power [IOTAP]
abstract: Complex SOC Implementation CAD tools have built-in Multi-Objective Optimization (MOO) algorithms to achieve optimal balance between Power, Performance and Area. However, there is always a scope of last-mile sub-optimality present in end design state for a variety of designs and tool dependency. With advancement of data science, analytics and AI, new research directions are emerging to recommend standard cell and interconnect parameters. This paper presents an automated sub-optimality characterization capability for signal interconnect using a multi-variate cost function. Auto-identified sub-optimal nets also get alternate best-fit track assignment guidance and incremental re-routing executed in a scalable streamlined flow. 15+ Design trials in 3 tech nodes indicate 4-10% Timing and 0.53 % power improvement potential with 60%+ success in trials.

title: Precision Clock Generation with Reference Clock Loss Tolerant Dynamic Tuning to Enable Crystal Less SSD
abstract: SSD (Solid State Drives) controllers communicate between hosts with high-speed interface like PCIe and NAND flash arrays. It gets data from host and transfer them to NAND and vice versa. To perform these operations, the controller needs highly accurate high-speed clocks for sustained performance. These clocks are generated by a clock multiplier circuit like PLL which requires an accurate reference clock. In general, a crystal oscillator (XTAL) is used to provide it, but it incurs BOM cost and increases PCB design complexity. Though the host transmits a clean clock along with the data, it may turn it off before the controller has finished transferring the data to NAND. This work presents a novel design by which this host clock is multiplexed with an internal relaxation oscillator clock to always provide a clock to the PLL. The control logic ensures that the output clock is always available by selecting between the input clock and the internal clock without any external indication and any frequency glitch. Thus, the PLL runs at highest accuracy when new data is coming in and is available at a lower accuracy to complete back-end operations when data stops. This enables the SSD to remove the XTAL and reduce the cost and complexity. The design was implemented in TSMC 7nm with 0.036 mm2 core area and was validated in lab.

title: TRANSPOSE: Circuit Transformations for Power Side-Channel Security at Register Transfer Level
abstract: Power Side-Channel Attacks (PSCAs) are a significant threat to modern cryptographic hardware. The overall power consumption of the target device can be passively probed to obtain the secrets being processed by its underlying cryptographic algorithm. Several countermeasures have been formulated to secure hardware implementations of cryptographic algorithms against such attacks. The objective of such countermeasures is to reduce the correlation between secret data being processed and the power consumption (the side-channel) of the device under attack. In this work, we propose an automated, circuit transformation-based ad-hoc countermeasure against PSCAs at the Register-Transfer Level (RTL). By analyzing sensitive registers within the device we propose a method that duplicates sub-circuits influencing the output of these sensitive registers. Additionally, register pushing and balancing, and clock gating are applied adequately to aid further obfuscation. As demonstrated through our experiments on the state-of-the-art ciphers PRESENT and AES's S-boxes, these approaches were found to be quite effective in randomizing the power consumption and reducing the dynamic power consumption of the circuits. Standard TVLA test of our protected circuits against the unprotected implementations show a significant increase in the effort for univariate PSCA attacks.

title: DuRTL - Information Flow Analysis Tool for Register Transfer Level Hardware Designs
abstract: In this tool paper, we present a design information flow analysis tool called DuRTL. DuRTL is an open-source hardware information flow analysis tool implemented in C++ that helps designers understand and comprehend unknown hardware designs written in Verilog and VHDL. DuRTL implements an approach for Hardware Information Flow Tracking based on a tagging mechanism where unique tags are injected into a hardware design. Each tag is associated with a signal at a specific time and identifies a flow of information during the traversal of the circuit. We explain the methodology and IFT implementation of DuRTL and some of the design choices made during the development. We also present some experiments that show the capabilities of DuRTL.

title: An SRAM-Based Multi-Operand Architecture Implementing Multi-Bit Boolean Functions Using in-Memory Periphery Computing
abstract: This paper introduces a highly scalable in-memory computing architecture for implementing (1) $M$-operand, $N$-bit Boolean functions, viz., AND/NAND/NOR/OR, (2) any arbitrary Boolean function expressed as the sum of products (e.g., F=AB'CD+ABC'D'), (3) $N$ parallel 2-bit XOR operations. Our technique performs operations using a modified 9T SRAM cell-based peripheral circuitry near the SRAM array. Unlike conventional 9T SRAM designs that use the same bitlines for both read and write operations, our design introduces dedicated read lines to separate the read and write paths. This separation improves efficiency and allows in-memory implementation of complex Boolean operations. To implement $M$ -operand, $N$ -bit AND/OR operations, the periphery circuit has $N$ compute blocks, each with $M$ columns. The compute block stores the input operands along with configuration bits to choose the correct operation. An equality checker circuit compares the input operands with configuration bits to obtain original or complemented input. The outputs of equality checkers of different columns are connected to a product line, and by DeMorgan's theorem, either AND/NAND or NOR/OR can be realized. Using TSMC 65nm PDK in Cadence Virtuoso, we have demonstrated 64-bit AND/NAND/OR/NOR operations and 64 parallel 2-bit XOR operations. At 0.7V VDD, our design consumes 24.5fJ/bit and operates at 660MHz for XOR operations and 384MHz for other operations.

title: MAGIC-Based High-Speed Adders for in-Memory Computing Using Memristors
abstract: In-memory computing circuits are built-in memristive crossbar arrays using MAGIC and IMPLY logic styles. A semi-serial full adder is proposed using MAGIC logic, takes ten computational steps and can be implemented in a $3\times 7$ crossbar. This paper proposes two designs of RCA using MAGIC style, both of which are optimized to take fewer steps through parallel processing in different rows/columns. Both designs are $2\times$ faster than existing MAGIC-based RCA designs. In particular, the proposed 32-bit RCA using serial and semi-serial full adder takes 199 and 232 steps, respectively. The proposed designs are implemented on a crossbar with efficient use of memristors along the crossbar. The performance has been evaluated through simulations of the RCA designs using VTEAM model of memristor.

title: OwlsEye: Real-Time Low-Light Video Instance Segmentation on Edge and Exploration of Fixed-Posit Quantization
abstract: Video Instance Segmentation (VIS) in low light conditions presents a significant challenge when deployed on resource-constrained edge devices, especially in autonomous vehicles, surveillance, robotics, or similar applications. This paper presents OwlsEye, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first hardware implementation for real-time Video Instance Segmentation under low-light settings using an off-the-shelf RGB camera. Implemented on the Intel Nezha Embedded platform, OwlsEye demonstrates an improvement in Frames Per Second (FPS) from 0.6 to 28 FPS using model weight quantization, brightness verification, and asynchronous FIFO Pipelining. This paper also presents the EQyTorch framework, an extension of Qtorch+ for fixed-posit numbers, used in weight quantization for the YOLOv8 architecture. We show that fixed-posit quantization achieves an improvement in latency and power utilization of $2.35\times, 3.6\times$, and $9.02\times, 87.91\times$ compared to INT8 and FP32 for 65nm CMOS. Furthermore, this paper presents a synthetic DarkCOCO2017 validation dataset to test the OwlsEye segmentation performance in enhanced, original, and dark images. Our work highlights a novel real-time low-light VIS system and the potential of using Fixed-Posit quantization for edge AI applications.

title: RISC-V Based Secure Processor Architecture for Return Address Protection
abstract: RISC-V-based cores are increasingly becoming pop-ular in embedded system applications because of their open-source architecture. Protecting such systems against memory-based attacks is one of the most difficult challenge. Buffer over-flow (BFO) attacks, specifically on Stack, can alter the program execution flow and are extensively employed by attackers. RISC-V foundation is working on specifications that will be used to maintain the control flow integrity (CFI) of the overall system. It will add ‘zicfiss’ and ‘zicfiip’ extensions for both backward edge and forwarded edge CFI, respectively. We propose a hardware-based approach that uses existing Return Address Stack (RAS) and requires low overhead, minimal microarchitecture changes, and limited software overhead to protect against such attacks. We assessed the performance of our design using buffer-intensive benchmarks. We verified its security by subjecting it to evaluation with the RIPE benchmark and our in-house test cases for BFO check. This approach safeguards the system from BFO attacks and could also enhance its security against Spectre attacks that exploit RAS vulnerabilities. We validated our design with Rocket-Core-based SoC and found less than 0.1% memory overhead and 2% timing overhead from the best case.

title: NSGA-RM: NSGA-II Evolved Performance Optimized Non-Homogeneous Recursive Polynomial Multiplier Architectures
abstract: Implementing hardware-efficient and high-performance polynomial multiplication in finite fields is crucial for enhancing crypto-systems on silicon, which is desirable for system-on-chip (SoC) applications. The recent developments, such as hybrid recursive multiplier (HRM) design leverage state-of-the-art various (SOTA) multipliers, M-Term Non-Homogeneous Karatsuba Multiplier (MNHKA), and M-Term Non-Homogeneous Overlap-Free Karatsuba Polynomial Multiplier (MNHOKA). However, HRM design explores the design space heuristically, which may not always yield optimal solutions. To overcome this limitation, a novel Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm Recursive Multiplier (NSGA-II-RM) technique is proposed over exhaustive design space exploration to achieve the most optimal solution. By applying NSGA-II optimization technique, the design process systematically explores a wide array of potential recursive-multiplier (RM) configurations, across multiple contrasting hardware parameters. The design solutions generated through multiple runs of NSGA-II algorithm are synthesized using the Cadence Genus tool for GPDK 45nm technology node. The best Optimal-front solution offers a 24.65% footprint saving, a 6.71% improves critical path delay, area-delay-product (ADP) gain of 29.71%, power savings of 40.65%, and a salient 34.32% improvement in Power-Per-Area (PPA) compared to the cutting-edge designs of MNHKA, MNHOKA, and HRM. All the design files are made freely available for easy adoption and further usage to the researchers and designers community.

title: Tunnel Magnetoresistance in Strained L10-FeAu Perpendicular Magnetic Tunnel Junction
abstract: In this study, we have analyzed intermetallic $\mathrm{L}{1_{0}}\text{-}$ FeAu alloy-based magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) using Non-Equilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) technique in combination with Density Functional Theory (DFT), and performed a strain analysis to ascertain the influence of strain on its tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR). Our findings reveal that the unstrained $\mathrm{L}{1_{0}}-\text{FeAu}$ ferromagnet shows significantly high TMR because of the spin-polarized $\Delta _{1}$ bands on the Fermi surface. However, on applying strain, TMR has dropped in both tensile and compressive strain, as compared to the unstrained case. Our detailed analysis shows that there is a change in the spin-polarized bands at the Fermi surface under strain that leads to an overall reduction in TMR. These findings highlight the impact of strain on TMR of FeAu-based MTJs and provide valuable insights into its utilization in spintronic applications.

title: Optimal Respiratory Rate Estimation with mmWave Sensing Using PYNQ System-on-Chip Platform
abstract: This paper propose a non-invasive method for range estimation and monitoring of human respiration rate using mmWave sensing on PYNQ platform. The approach employs Range Fast Fourier Transform (RFFT), phase extraction and unwrapping, FIR filtering, and is followed by multiple respiration rate (RR) estimation techniques and their optimal weighted combination over quadratic cost function on the PYNQ board. Results on the PYNQ show ~199.2% accuracy for range detection and ~194.5% accuracy for RR estimation. The developed model can be deployed on a portable embedded system for RR measurement.

title: Physical Insights into the Leakage Mechanisms Governing the Scaling Trends in 4H-SiC Based Junctionless FETs
abstract: The lateral Band-to-band tunneling (L-BTBT) has been extensively studied in Silicon Junctionless field effect transistors (JLFETs) as the dominant leakage mechanism. However, the same analysis does not hold true for wide bandgap materials like 4H-SiC, since as the recent studies show, for lower drain bias the L-BTBT is not triggered in 4H-SiC JLFETs. Therefore, in this paper, for the first time, we present a comprehensive analysis of the various leakage mechanisms governing the subthreshold performance of the 4H-SiC based ultra-short channel planar junctionless (JL) FETs. Using well-calibrated 2-D device simulations, our study gives physical insights into the three main leakage components in JLFETs: i) Gate induced drain leakage (GIDL) mechanism ii) direct gate tunneling, and (iii) inefficient volume depletion. Unlike the silicon-based JLFETs which are significantly impacted by the L-BTBT induced GIDL, the 4H-SiC JLFETs are quite immune to the L-BTBT induced GIDL due to their wider bandgap compared to the silicon. However, the leakage mechanism in 4H-SiC can essentially be dictated either by the gate leakage due to the direct tunneling through the thin gate dielectric or the inefficient volume depletion especially for the sub-10 nm regime. Therefore, we have presented the design guidelines for sub-10 nm regime, which can be used for designing required channel length, channel thickness, and gate oxide thickness to have the effective volume depletion. Our comprehensive analysis reveals essential findings that can help in developing and adopting the 4H-SiC based JLFETs at advanced technology nodes, especially for low power and low leakage applications, like Internet of Things (IoT) and automotive applications.

title: Advancing Neural Network Performance with Probabilistic Computing for ReLU Function
abstract: Probabilistic computing (using p-bits), based on stochastic computing, can operate in an invertible mode, enabling bidirectional operations. This functionality addresses significant challenges, improves neural network training, and opens new possibilities in neural networks. This article presents a framework and robust approach for designing p-circuits of logic circuits using p-bits to enhance probabilistic computing. This paper presents the design of a 2 × 1 multiplexer, a two-input non-imply logic gate (AB), and a ReLU activation function using the Hamiltonian method. Further, this paper presents two designs of ReLU, one using AND gate while the second design uses a non-imply logic gate. The non-imply gate based ReLU requires fewer number of p-bits. In particular, a 10-bit ReLU takes 20 p-bits, with ten inputs and ten outputs. Further, the proposed approach results the design with a lower graph density of 0.26 for the 5-bit proposed ReLU, whereas the best existing design has a graph density of 0.45. The proposed p-circuits were simulated, and results demonstrate the invertible nature of the p-circuits,

title: Advancing Rehabilitation Through Low Weight Hand Assistive System: Design and Impact Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a Smart Hand Mobility As-sistive Device designed to aid individuals with impaired hand function due to conditions such as stroke, spinal cord injuries, and neuromuscular disorders. The device enhances daily activities and provides comprehensive rehabilitation support. Leveraging advanced sensor technology, real-time data processing, and adaptive actuation, it detects and amplifies subtle finger movements, facilitating precise hand motions. Unlike conventional methods that are often slow and lack real-time feedback, the proposed design solution offers immediate functional assistance and pro-gressive rehabilitative training. The device integrates seamlessly with a user-centric mobile application offering predefined phys-iotherapy exercises tailored to individual needs. Additionally, the application includes interactive games that engage users in therapeutic activities to improve motor skills and cognitive functions. Experimental evaluations assess the device's efficacy in enhancing grip strength, dexterity, and overall hand function. The system also features multiple control modes, allowing users to select from manual assistance, cyclic movement training, or task-specific routines. Through this approach, our device aspires to significantly elevate the quality of life for individuals with hand mobility impairments, positioning itself as a transformative tool in assistive technology and rehabilitative care.

title: HapticGuide: Interactive Wearable Braille Guide for Enhancing Visual Education
abstract: This paper introduces a novel haptic wearable Braille guide designed to enhance the educational experience for visually impaired students by enabling them to trace and understand geometric shapes. Traditional methods like tactile graphics and physical models are often limited in providing dynamic, real-time feedback, which is essential for grasping complex spatial concepts. To address these limitations, the pro-posed device integrates a 15 × 15 grid touch screen made from Velostat pressure sensors and copper strips, a wearable glove equipped with five coin vibration motors, and a cloud-based synchronization system. This system allows students to receive real-time, directional haptic feedback, guiding them as they trace shapes, thereby improving their spatial understanding and cognitive mapping skills. The device is designed to be economical, portable, and easy to use, making it accessible for classroom and remote learning environments. By offering a more interactive and adaptable solution, this device advances the current state of assistive technology for visually impaired learners. It provides a scalable and effective tool for enhancing geometric education. The paper details this innovative educational aid's design, functionality, and potential applications.

title: Startup Circuit for Relaxation Oscillators with Low Functional Current and Minimal Area
abstract: This paper presents a novel start up technique for low current, low area, closed loop relaxation oscillator. In the proposed implementation, start-up time is improved by keeping the circuit initially in open loop and then in closed loop when the frequency is settled. In open loop mode, current is injected in the ring oscillator to charge the internal nodes. This results in approximately 3x improvement in start-up time (from 466us to 150us) across process, voltage, and temperature variations. This is achieved without increasing the functional current of the oscillator which consumes 52 nanoamperes of current. The start-up circuit is implemented by using current mirrors and digital circuits which do not require large area and offer very less leakage current. Proposed circuit is implemented in 16FFC technology for a 32KHz, 94nW relaxation oscillator circuit. The circuit operates on 1.8V (+/−10%) supply voltage and over a temperature range of-40°C to 125°C. The oscillator circuit shows +/− 5% post trim frequency variation across voltage and temperature.

title: Optimization of Sub-Threshold Standard Cells for Energy Efficient Designs
abstract: Energy efficiency is a critical focus in contemporary integrated circuit (IC) design, particularly for ultra-low power applications. Subthreshold voltage scaling presents a promising solution for reducing energy consumption, though it introduces performance challenges that necessitate custom design libraries. This work presents a comprehensive methodology for creating a specialized subthreshold standard cell library, utilizing the SPEA-2 genetic algorithm for optimal transistor sizing.1 Our library demonstrates an average improvement in energy efficiency of 44% compared to conventional approaches. We validate its performance by synthesizing RISC-V processors and EPFL benchmark circuits, comparing them with standard foundry libraries operating at nominal (1.2 V) and near-threshold (600 mV) voltages. The results show a 13.26× and 1.49× reduction in energy consumption, respectively, for the subthreshold library. However, this comes with a 5.21× and 1.3× increase in area, respectively. These findings underscore the viability of subthreshold libraries as an effective option for energy-constrained designs.

title: PAF-Enc: Position Affine Encoding to Reduce Bit-Flips in Non-Volatile Main Memories
abstract: Adaptability issues of DRAM with modern dataintensive workloads make their scalability difficult. Emerging non-volatile memories (NVMs) can be helpful in this regard due to their density and low energy consumption. However, NVM's lifetime and performance are severely impacted by its writes. Disparity in the stored data and the data to be written at that place contributes to the write operations. With this insight, we propose an encoding technique that eliminates most of the upcoming bit writes by increasing the resemblance between the newly arrived cacheblock data and memory data. Our proposal PAF-Enc operates in two stages where it begins with analyzing the memory data patterns to generate masks resembling them. This is followed by encoding the incoming cacheblocks with these masks using a simple XOR operation to bring it closer to the memory data prior to the memory write. Our encoding technique is lightweight, offers significant bit write reduction, and boosts longevity and performance, as indicated by experimental data.

title: TOGGLE6.0: A 4.8Gbps Next Generation Area and Power Efficient Transceiver for Flash Memory Interface
abstract: Flash memory interfaces transfer data to and from universal flash storage (UFS) devices used in mobile phones, where there is demand for high-speed designs with low area and pad capacitance. Toggle6.0 is a next generation NAND IO memory interface introduced for memory transfers at 4.8Gbps data rate. In this paper, we propose a scalable architecture using thin-oxide devices to reduce the pad capacitance and an elevated ground voltage generator to reduce the device stress for the driver, and a current-based equalization scheme that can be extended to multiple taps with less area overhead and a per-receiver VREF-based tuning scheme to improve READ mode timing margin for the receiver. The proposed design is compared with the existing design in terms of power, performance and area. The proposed architecture reduces driver area and pad capacitance by 42.47% and 23% and power on average by 24.65% in lower power mode. Receiver eye margin is improved by 15% and area is reduced by 10.29 %.

title: CMOSP18 FD-SOI Technology Based MCU Achieving High Performance of 1.2GHz Using High Speed, Optimized Leakage & High Density Tightly Coupled Memory (TCM)
abstract: Tightly coupled memories (TCM) are high performance memories which dictate the overall performance of a processor. Physically these embedded memories are present very close to the processors and any enhancement in these memories benefits the processor. Two variants of memory instances were developed to achieve better performance as well as leakage for the processor core in CMOSP18 technology. The memory instances which will be placed farther from the processor core were optimized for performance while ones which will be placed closer to the processor core were optimized for leakage with minimal impact in performance. Both the memory variants were developed using high density bitcell to reduce area and hence the RC delay associated between processor core and memory leading to overall gain in performance. On benchmarking the design with respect to competitor TCM design substantial gain was observed in all metrics - performance(reduction in access + setuptime by 16%), leakage(reduced by 33%) and area(reduced by 17%).

title: Multi-Object Detection Through Meta-Training in Resource-Constrained UAV-Based Surveillance Applications
abstract: This work focuses on implementing You Look Only Once (YOLO) models on resource-constraint devices with improved generalization, for drone imagery-based multi-object detection. The generalization improvement has been done using a proposed meta-training framework. The proposed meta-training is an aspect of transfer learning that focuses on domain generalization (or adaptation) through learning a variety of domains using transfer learning. Herein, different domains have distinct tasks with adversaries such as object detection in the nighttime, crowds, sunny weather, and small object areas, the model is learning to adapt to the next domain iteratively through a gradient descent-based optimization. Three different configurations of YOLO, publicly available data, and custom-made data are involved in validating the improved generalization. Each model has been trained on a big fraction of both datasets one by one, and predictions have been taken within both datasets. The average precision (AP) values and other visual results have been calculated in various cases to demonstrate enhanced multi-object detection. Furthermore, the model has been deployed on three commercially available resource-constrained devices. The related codes are available on GitHub: https://github.com/vy0123/Yolov8_drone_vision.git.

title: Hardware Implementation of Blind Decoding of Downlink Control Information for 5G
abstract: The user equipment (UE) based on the fifthgeneration new radio wireless communication technology standardized by 3GPP receives downlink control information (DCI) to obtain the time-frequency resources, modulation order, code rate, etc required for decoding the received data. The location of the resources containing the DCI will not be directly known to the UE instead it is received in certain possible locations informed through signaling. The UE must blindly decode multiple DCIs with different lengths from the different possible locations within a very stringent time limit of the order of 0.25 ms. This involves time consuming exhaustive search and imposes significant computation load to identify the locations for decoding multiple DCIs. In this paper, a flexible hardware implementation to perform the blind decoding (BD) within the time limit is proposed. It is found that the decoding is completed within 65% of the time available for BD by utilizing optimal resources. The proposed implementation is tested and validated for its functionality and performance using the in-house 5G testbed implemented using the Zynq Ultrascale + RFSoC ZCU111 board from Xilinx by integrating into an existing UE receive chain.
